subject: POC environment choices & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Catherine Taylor <c.taylor@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC environment choices & acceptance criteria

Hi Catherine —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and timeline for the POC.

What we heard on the call
- Primary goal: validate an automated clinical summary workflow for discharge notes with PHI in scope.
- Key constraints: data cannot leave your VPC/approved regions; vendor security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence required before demo ingestion.
- Success stakeholders: Clinical AI team (evaluation), Security (approve data flows), Procurement (terms).

Recommended POC approaches (tradeoffs)
1) Hosted trial (fastest onboarding)
   - Pros: no infra setup, Redwood handles model serving, 48–72h dev sandbox ready.
   - Cons: not suitable if PHI cannot leave your VPC; we offer encrypted linkages but won't meet strict VPC-only requirements.
2) Dedicated sandbox (Redwood Dedicated, isolated GPU pool)
   - Pros: predictable performance, can be region-restricted and isolated per-customer. Good middle ground for sensitive workloads when VPC is not available yet.
   - Cons: requires a short provisioning window (3–7 business days) and a small reserved commitment.
3) VPC-hosted Private deployment (recommended if PHI must remain inside your network)
   - Pros: customer-managed network, full data residency and KMS integration.
   - Cons: longer setup (2–4 weeks typical with procurement & infra coordination), we'll provide an ops runbook.

Suggested path for MediCore given constraints
- Start with a limited Dedicated sandbox POC (Redwood Dedicated) for functional validation and latency/throughput baselining while Security completes the VPC onboarding paperwork. If Security confirms VPC requirement early, we pause data ingestion and switch to a remote test harness.

POC success criteria (proposed, please adjust)
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 300ms for a 512-token request on the targeted model family.
- Throughput: sustain 15 req/sec with concurrent users (3 internal evaluators).
- Quality: automated summary F1 >= 0.82 against curated test set of 200 notes + qualitative clinician acceptability >= 4/5 on sample of 20.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence provided; data pipeline accepts encrypted S3 with customer-managed KMS or direct VPC peering before PHI ingestion.

High-level timeline (target)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize POC option and scope, sign simple SOW / mutual action plan.
- Week 1: Dedicated sandbox provisioned; initial onboarding call; secure credential exchange.
- Week 2: Ingest sample dataset (anonymized first if Security needs it) and run baseline tests.
- Week 3: Iteration on prompts/response templates and throughput tuning.
- Week 4: Joint review, provide final report + next-step recommendation (Dedicated -> Prod or VPC cutover).

Ownership (proposed)
- Redwood: Ben (sales) — overall POC coordination; Marissa — trial ops & infra; Rachel — solution engineer and prompt tuning.
- MediCore: Catherine — product lead; Security — approvals; Procurement — contract & billing.

Immediate asks
1) Confirm preferred POC environment (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC) — based on call notes we recommend Dedicated as a pragmatic starting point.
2) Share target test set (or timeline for access) and any procurement constraints.
3) Confirm a 30–45 minute kickoff window next week (I propose Wed 12/8 10:00–10:45 PT).

I've attached a draft POC quote and a trial ops checklist for your internal review. If you want, we can redact PHI-related steps until Security signs off.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Catherine Taylor <c.taylor@medicorehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medicorehealth.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC environment choices & acceptance criteria

Ben — thanks for the detailed recap. A few clarifications from Security/Product/Procurement perspective: 

1) PHI requirement: Our security policy requires PHI to remain in our VPC unless the vendor is listed on our managed vendor stack. At minimum we need a VPC option or guaranteed bring-your-own-key setup where keys never leave our control.
2) Timeline: Procurement has an internal deadline to complete vendor selection by 12/22; we need the POC to be completed and reviewed with security by 12/17 to make the cut. Is that feasible if we go Dedicated?
3) Success criteria: clinical team is happy with the F1 target, but we also need a measurable latency baseline relative to current rule-based pipeline (aim: <= 2x current latency).

We prefer Dedicated if we can get an accelerated provisioning and a strict KMS contract rider. Would Marissa be the contact for the Dedicated provisioning timeline? Also looping procurement on the email thread so they can review the quote and flag any requirements.

Catherine Taylor
Head of Data Science, MediCore Health
c.taylor@medicorehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Catherine Taylor <c.taylor@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@medicorehealth.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC environment choices & acceptance criteria

Thanks — super helpful context. Short answers inline, and next steps below.

1) PHI & keys: We can support BYOK (customer-managed KMS) with Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we can provide envelope encryption but that won't satisfy your VPC-only policy.
2) Timeline feasibility: We can compress the Dedicated provisioning to 3 business days if procurement sign-off and required paperwork are completed this week. That should allow the POC to complete by 12/17 if we run an aggressive cadence (Week 1 provision + baseline, Week 2 tuning + report). We'll add a few days buffer in the Ops checklist.
3) Latency baseline: We'll run parallel tests against your rule-based API during Week 2 to produce the relative latency metric (target: <= 2x current).

Requested immediate steps
- Marissa: can you confirm a fast-provisioning path and estimated earliest window if we get SOW by EOD Friday?
- Catherine / Procurement: please confirm acceptance of the draft quote (attached) or list changes; if acceptable, procurement can sign the SOW + standard KMS rider.
- Catherine: please share a small sample set (anonymized) or allow placeholder synthetic data for Week 1 so we can show progress; we will not ingest real PHI until Security signs the KMS/VPC rider.

I've re-attached the POC quote and a one-page SOW excerpt for quick review.

— Ben

Attachments: redwood-poc-quote-DEC2027.pdf, poc-sow-excerpt-DEC2027.pdf
